rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 3 "Read for the decisions that matter": line 39 header says "Read"; line 43: "Scan for the decisions most likely to change the work: files, design, assumptions, and verification." — the chunk's own body instructs scanning, not reading, contradicting its header verb. This is the exact read-vs-scan defect vocabulary.md documents ("read a short artifact end-to-end... scan a long one for the parts that matter") and that this file's own maintainer block records as already fixed at a sibling heading (line 128-129: "Header was Read the plan… until 2026-08-12" — but that fix landed on the chunk-4 header "## Scan the plan before you push back", not this chunk-3 header, which still reads "Read for the decisions that matter").
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Retitle chunk 3's header to use "Scan" (or otherwise match the body's own scanning instruction), mirroring the fix already applied to chunk 4's header.

Considered chunk 4's three consecutive "Notice which..." sentences (lines 48-49) as a possible anaphora triple; each leg carries distinct concrete content (file-naming, verification steps, assumptions) mirroring chunk 3's named axes, so treated as deliberate scanning-checklist structure rather than a tic. No "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction, no self-grading superlative, no number-with-retraction, no empty-leg verb triplet found.
